title: Hosted Endpoint Readiness: scope hedging, acceptance gates, and go-live playbook
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description: This ticket is the canonical PRD + go-live playbook for a consolidated hosted endpoint launch covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank surfaces. The goal is to ship a minimal, consistent behavioral surface that developers can rely on for production inference while preserving operational controls that allow us to hedge scope during the cutover. This doc defines the required behavior, what is explicitly out-of-scope for the initial tranche, acceptance gates, and an operationalized cutover plan (canary, metrics, rollback).
scope_clarifications:
1) Chat: initial launch will support single-turn and multi-turn via client-managed conversation state; server-side conversation history stitching (ephemeral context stitching) is out-of-scope.
2) Completions: support streaming and non-streaming modes with token-level billing parity. Structured output schemas (strong types) will be soft-gated and evaluated in a follow-up.
3) Embeddings: Vector size and normalization follow cataloged model variants; embedding-only endpoints will be rate-limited to prevent noisy high-throughput abuse.
4) Rerank: provide scored list reranking for top-K candidates; full retrieval pipeline integration will be demonstrated with a sample reference app but not enforced for all customers.
5) Billing/quotas: per-token and per-embedding usage reporting required at the token-level; detailed cost breakdown per-route will be a post-launch enhancement.
acceptance_criteria:
A. Behavioral correctness:
- Chat and completions return outputs matching the interaction contract for at least 95% of a 500-sample behavioral test set (prompt + expected properties).
- Embeddings stable (cosine similarity drift < 0.5% vs baseline for 1000 anchor comparisons).
- Rerank ordering correlation (Kendall tau) >= 0.75 vs reference ranker on the designated eval set.
B. Performance & reliability:
- Baseline latency: median < 120ms for small completions (<= 64 tokens), p99 < 450ms under steady baseline load.
- Throughput SLO: sustain configured dedicated lane throughput for canary traffic profile for 30m without dropped requests.
- Error rate: production error rate < 0.5% for canary slice.
C. Observability & telemetry:
- Token-level cost and latency telemetry emitted and visible in Console dashboards.
- Per-route tracing enabled with sample traces for chat and rerank flows.
D. Safety & guardrails:
- Safety filters (policy hooks) integrated in request pipeline with blocking/flagging behavior consistent with the policy matrix.
E. Ops readiness:
- Runbooks for canary cutover, rollback, and rapid mitigation exist and are validated by a dry-run with on-call.
F. Security & compliance:
- KMS integration validated for tenant keys used in Private/Dedicated trials; audit logs enabled for host-admin actions.
(G) Release gating: All items above green in the canary window and no open P0 regressions.
go_live_playbook: Pre-cutover: freeze surface changes 48 hours before canary start; ensure all PRs merged and tagged to hosted-2026.03 branch.
Step 1 - Canary bootstrap (T0): route 1% of internal and 1% of public beta traffic to new surface; monitor telemetry for 15 minutes.
Step 2 - Canary ramp (T0+15m): if canary metrics healthy, increment to 5% for 30 minutes; verify latency, error-rate, and behavioral regression dashboards.
Step 3 - Canary extended (T0+45m): hold at 10% for 60 minutes and run full regression suites (behavioral + embeddings stability).
Step 4 - Gradual percentage ramp: increase to 25% then 50% over 3 hours while keeping a shadow of old endpoints for A/B drift analysis.
Step 5 - Full cutover: after 4-hour steady-state with no P0s, change routing policy to treat hosted-2026.03 as default for green lanes and monitor for 6 hours.
Rollback criteria: trigger immediate rollback to previous deployed model if p99 latency increases > 2x baseline OR error rate exceeds 1.5% OR behavioral fail rate on gating suite > 5%.
Post-cutover: 24-hour watch with daily summary to product, eng, and SRE; schedule post-launch retro and open a follow-up ticket for scope items deferred.
launch_checklist: Docs: PRD and quickstart updated in Confluence and docs.redwood.ai; include sample requests for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
SDKs: Node/Python SDKs updated with endpoint signatures and streaming for completions; tests added in package CI.
Telemetry: dashboards created (per-route latency, token-cost, p95/p99), alerts configured for error-rate and regression signals.
E2E Tests: behavioral regression suite (500 prompts), embeddings stability harness (1k anchors), rerank correlation suite (2 datasets) passing in CI.
Runbooks: canary, rollback, and emergency mitigation runbooks published and smoke-tested with on-call.
Security: KMS keys validated for private trials, audit logging enabled, SSO and tenant RBAC sanity checked.
Billing: per-token usage breakdown available in billing UI and tested with simulated workloads.
Compliance: data retention config options present; PII redaction / policy hooks validated against sample data.
Samples & Reference App: a lightweight reference app demonstrating chat + retrieval + rerank integration deployed to staging.
Stakeholder comms: launch window announced; support rota and escalation paths shared with GTM and support teams.
risk_and_mitigations:
Risk 1: Behavioral regressions missed by limited eval sets -> Mitigation: expand canary evals to cover 6 high-variance prompt buckets and run small human-in-the-loop checks during canary.
Risk 2: Unexpected token-cost spikes -> Mitigation: enable per-tenant hard rate-limits and a temporary cost throttle path that routes to a lower-cost quantized model.
Risk 3: Latency regressions at scale -> Mitigation: staged traffic ramp, pre-warm cache paths (ephemeral KV), and fast-fail fallbacks to simpler model variants.
Risk 4: Security misconfig for private tenants -> Mitigation: gated private onboarding with checklist and mandatory KMS proof-of-possession.
rollout_strategy: We will use a graded canary with several safety nets: internal dogfooding (internal traffic), invited beta customers, public canary, then full. Each stage includes a behavior regression pass and a short human review window. For high-risk tenants we will offer an opt-in delayed cutover with an enforced traffic cap for the first 7 days. Fallback policies: per-route fallback mapping to compatible quantized variants or older model revisions; a global emergency switch to route all traffic to the previous stable branch.
quality_checks: Behavioral regression: 500 curated prompts covering conversation continuity, role instructions, and few-shot patterns.
Embeddings drift: nightly job comparing new embeddings to baseline vectors for drift detection; anomaly alert threshold at 1% drift rate.
Rerank correlation: weekly automated Kendall tau and MAP checks vs baseline datasets.
Perf: synthetic load tests to validate p99 latency targets at projected canary QPS plus 20% headroom.
Security: automated smoke for KMS operations and audit log generation during deploys.
